summary:
**Planetary Analog Finder** is an interactive scientific platform designed to identify Earth environments that share measurable characteristics with selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

We developed a platform that allows users to explore planetary regions, select terrestrial locations, and compare their characteristics through a dedicated Scientific Comparison Studio. Our approach focuses on scientific parameters such as topography, terrain morphology, surface temperature, geology, and surface materials. By leveraging scientific data from the resources provided in the challenge, the platform aims to transform complex planetary observations into accessible and meaningful comparisons.

Our solution addresses the challenge by helping researchers identify potential terrestrial analog sites where certain planetary conditions can be studied and where exploration technologies, instruments, and equipment can be tested before future space missions.

details:
Planetary Analog Finder

Earth · Moon · Mars — Discover Earth. Understand Other Worlds.

Planetary Analog Finder is an interactive scientific platform designed to help identify Earth environments that share measurable characteristics with selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

The platform allows users to explore planetary regions, discover their characteristics, and compare them with terrestrial environments through a dedicated Scientific Comparison Studio. Users can select a planetary body, explore available regions, choose an Earth location, and examine relevant scientific parameters such as terrain, topography, geology, surface temperature, environmental conditions, and surface materials.

Our approach focuses on making planetary science more accessible by bringing different types of scientific observations into one interactive environment. The long-term objective is to support meaningful comparisons using reliable data from the space agency resources provided in the challenge. Comparisons must account for data availability, measurement quality, uncertainty, and the limitations of reproducing extraterrestrial conditions on Earth.

Benefits and intended impact

Testing equipment and technologies directly on the Moon or Mars is expensive and difficult. Certain environments on Earth can provide useful testing conditions for instruments, exploration technologies, and scientific experiments. Our platform aims to help researchers discover these potential terrestrial analog environments, organize relevant information, and understand both similarities and differences between locations.

The intended impact is to support scientific research, improve preparation for future robotic and human exploration missions, and make planetary data easier to explore and interpret.

Technology and tools

  • Frontend: React and JavaScript
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Database: SQLite
  • Data management: SQLAlchemy
  • Visualization: Interactive maps and 3D planetary visualization
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub

Creativity and design considerations

The creative aspect of Planetary Analog Finder is its combination of planetary exploration and terrestrial comparison in a single interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying planetary images or scientific information, the project is designed around a practical research workflow: explore a planetary region, select a terrestrial environment, and investigate their measurable characteristics.

During development, we considered scientific reliability, data accessibility, geographical accuracy, usability, performance, and the limitations of Earth-based analog environments. We also considered the importance of distinguishing verified measurements from estimated or unavailable information.

Our vision: Understand Earth to better explore other worlds.
